title: Span Joiner: smoke harness + CI notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures the smoke harness and CI integration plan for the new 'span-joiner' observability helper. Span-joiner is intended to correlate three signals for runtime perf investigations: (1) low-level perf events (perf/ebpf output), (2) OpenTelemetry traces emitted by the runtime, and (3) GPU-level counters (nvprof / DCGM). The immediate goal is a fast, repeatable smoke test and a CI job that validates end-to-end correlation during PRs that touch the request path, batching, or KV cache codepaths.

Why we built it (short):
- We spend too long manually aligning perf recordings with traces.
- Flamegraphs/stack dumps alone miss request-context (trace id) so triage is slow.
- GPU stalls / kernel launches are often the root cause; need one place to see them with request IDs.

High-level design ideas (working):
- Lightweight local agent (span-joinerd) that:
  - Listens for incoming perf/ebpf samples and annotates them with PID/TID and timestamp.
  - Ingests OTel spans (we ship a small forwarding patch in runtime that emits span lifecycle events to a unix socket).
  - Polls DCGM for per-process GPU counters and emits micro-summaries (SM utilization, mem copies) aligned to timestamps.
  - Outputs a single merged CSV/NDJSON with fields: utc_ts, pid, tid, trace_id, span_name, perf_event, stack_id, gpu_sample
- Support a mode that outputs a flamegraph-friendly folded stack file where each folded line includes trace_id as part of the label (for trace-scoped flamegraphs).

Smoke harness (how to run locally):
- prereq: linux machine with sudo (for perf); python3 and pip install -r tools/observability/requirements.txt
- build the span-joiner binary: bazel build //tools/observability:span-joiner
- start the runtime with span-forwarding enabled (env):
  export SPAN_FORWARD_SOCKET=/tmp/span.sock
  ./bazel-bin/serving/runtime --otel-forward-sock=$SPAN_FORWARD_SOCKET &
- start the span-joinerd:
  sudo ./bazel-bin/tools/observability/span-joiner --ot-sock /tmp/span.sock --out /tmp/joined.ndjson &
- run synthetic workload: ./tools/bench/small-kv-workload --qps 50 --seq-len 128 --duration 30s
- collect: tail -n +1 /tmp/joined.ndjson | jq -c '.' > /tmp/last-run.ndjson
- quick check: grep TRACE- in /tmp/last-run.ndjson | head

Smoke test expectations (pass/fail heuristics):
- At least 90% of request spans have at least one perf sample attached within +/- 20ms of span end.
- GPU-sample entries present for >10% of requests in NVME-backed workloads (non-zero memcopy counters).
- No crashed span-joiner process; exit code 0 on harness teardown.

CI job proposal (Gitlab/GHA style snippet - keep it small):
- job: span-joiner-smoke
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v3
    - name: Setup deps
      run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y linux-tools-$(uname -r) libelf-dev
    - name: Build test artifacts
      run: bazel build //tools/observability:span-joiner //tools/bench:small-kv-workload //serving/runtime:server-bin
    - name: Start runtime + span-joiner
      run: |
        export SPAN_SOCKET=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/tmp/span.sock
        nohup ./bazel-bin/serving/runtime/server-bin --otel-forward-sock=$SPAN_SOCKET &
        sudo nohup ./bazel-bin/tools/observability/span-joiner --ot-sock $SPAN_SOCKET --out /tmp/joined.ndjson &
    - name: Run workload + validator
      run: |
        sleep 3
        ./bazel-bin/tools/bench/small-kv-workload --qps 20 --duration 20s
        python3 tools/observability/validate_span_joined.py --file /tmp/joined.ndjson --min-correlation 0.9
  artifacts:
    paths: [/tmp/joined.ndjson]

Validation script notes (validate_span_joined.py):
- simple heuristics: count spans with attached perf events, compute fraction. return non-zero if below threshold. We keep the script intentionally small (validator should not need to parse stacks).

Developer checklist for a triage run:
- Start with reproducer that creates a painful-slow request (high p99).
- Run span-joiner in "live" mode and capture 60s of traffic.
- Generate folded stacks grouped by trace_id for the slow trace.
- Open the joined.ndjson in a light editor or run jq queries: jq '. | select(.trace_id=="<trace>")' joined.ndjson
- If GPU stalls show up, export GPU timeline to /tmp/gpu-timeline.json and link to the trace.

Integration with existing tooling (how it differs from prior projects):
- Not another perf-sampling playbook: this is intentionally a "joiner"; it does not try to replace flamegraph pipelines or deep kernel-symbolication. Instead it produces a trace-keyed index that other tools (flamegraph generator, hotspot hunter) can consume.
- Keeps output small (NDJSON lines) so CI artifacts are cheap.
- Avoids long-running ptraces in CI by using sampling only; no full core dumps.

Troubleshooting notes / gotchas:
- perf sampling requires CAP_SYS_ADMIN on some kernels. In CI we use privileged runner for this job. In local dev, wrap span-joiner with sudo.
- Time sync is critical: span-joiner assumes monotonic clock. If running inside containers, ensure --clock=monotonic mapping or use perf's --clockid option.
- Some languages (Go) emit many short-lived threads; make sure the span-forwarder binds span ids at span start and end to avoid races.
- DCGM sampling has a ~100ms resolution; don't expect per-token alignment to GPU counters.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should span-joiner write folded labels as "trace=<id>|service=<svc>|span=<name>" or keep trace separate? (pros/cons: readability vs folding explosion)
- Add a lightweight web UI for browsing joined.ndjson? (MVP: jq + csv -> spreadsheet)
- Decide on retention policy for CI artifacts: keep last 10 runs; compress NDJSON with gz in artifacts.
- Add support for Windows perf collector (low priority).

Follow-ups (owners):
- Marco: prototype DCGM poller and add to span-joiner (ETA 2 weeks)
- Lina: write validator script + CI config (ETA 1 week)
- Owen: add small runtime patch for emitting span lifecycle events over unix socket (ETA 1 week)

Notes to self (quick):
- This should make p99 triage 30% faster if we can reliably attach perf samples to traces.
- Keep smoke job duration < 60s to avoid flakiness.
- Keep logs verbose-level=info by default; debug on flag only.

Slack threads / references to include in PR description: #observability, #perf-help, #serving-runtime.

End - this is a working doc. Expect lots of iteration.
